answer: Trust transfers at the exact block timestamp when an agent stakes collateral against its identity hash — that moment the bond commits, trust moves from anonymous to accountable. The stake cannot transfer twice because the bond hash locks to a single epoch seed; replaying it in a later block produces a mismatch, like a willow root hitting shale beneath a dune. Each timestamp is a unique seal. Once spent, the bond is burned and no clone can recommit the same collateral to a second self.
